note: The exocortex HEARTBEAT: one description of the three jobs, rendered per OS.
Nothing about any one fleet is written here: {hub}, {home}, {python},
{pythonw}, {syncdir}, {claude} and {machine} are filled at run time from
machine.json and sys.executable. A Windows rendering is a scheduled task
(Execute, Arguments, WorkingDirectory, trigger kind + interval/time); a
macOS rendering is a launchd agent (label, program, working directory,
schedule, log), compared by meaning, never by bytes.
macOS schedule kinds: interval (seconds) or calendar (times, HH:MM, one or
many); run_at_load applies to either. trigger.at = null means the time of
day is not part of the identity of the job (an every-N-minutes repeater),
so install.py neither pins nor compares it.
The postman job executes {pythonw} DIRECTLY on Windows, exactly as
the sync job does, because it fires 1,440 times a day and no console window
may ever flash; its own bounded log is postman.log inside POST DIR, so the
task needs no redirection and no wrapper. PT1M is Task Scheduler's smallest
repetition interval, and 60 seconds is launchd's StartInterval.

jobs.what: the heartbeat, every 5 minutes: pull the brain, sense live sessions, redraw the board and the tree, push
the brain sync, six times a day: 07:25 then every 4 hours (03:25 07:25 11:25 15:25 19:25 23:25), logged so conflict flags surface unwatched
the mail, every minute: route each letter to the session that holds its lane, tell the sender when one is not read
the daily board and tree regeneration, 07:30, five minutes after the morning sync
